title: OAuth apps
snippet:
OAuth 2.0 is an industry-standard authorization protocol that lets applications securely access Twilio APIs on your behalf, without sharing your Account SID and Auth Token or other long-lived API keys. Instead of using static credentials, your application exchanges a Client ID and Client Secret (or a user's approval) for a short-lived access token, which it then uses to make API calls. OAuth apps are how you set this up in Twilio — they keep your account credentials safe and give you fine-grained control over what each application can do.
Key benefits of using OAuth apps:
- **Short-lived access tokens** — OAuth credentials generate tokens with a limited lifespan, reducing the risk of credential leaks.
- **Scoped access** — Each token is restricted to a specific set of APIs, so an app only has access to what it needs.
OAuth apps can be created at both the account level and the organization level. See the links below to learn more about each:
- [Account OAuth apps](/docs/iam/oauth-apps/account-oauth-apps)
- [Organization OAuth apps](/docs/iam/oauth-apps/org-oauth-apps)

The Client Credentials grant ([RFC 6749, Section 4.4](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6749#section-4.4)) is designed for machine-to-machine (server-to-server) interactions, where an application authenticates as itself rather than on behalf of a user. This is the right choice for backend services, scheduled jobs, and internal tools.
**How it works:**
1. Create an OAuth app in the Twilio Console. Twilio generates a Client ID and Client Secret.
2. Your application sends these credentials to the Twilio OAuth token endpoint to request an access token.
3. Your application uses the access token to authenticate calls to Twilio APIs.
4. After the access token expires, use the Client ID and Client Secret to generate a new access token.
The Authorization Code grant ([RFC 6749, Section 4.1](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6749#section-4.1)) is designed for applications that access Twilio APIs on behalf of a user. It's most commonly used in web applications where users explicitly approve the access. Because the user must authenticate and consent, this grant offers stronger security than Client Credentials.
**How it works:**
1. Create an OAuth app with type Authorization Code to generate a Client ID, Client Secret, and Authorization URL.
2. Paste the Authorization URL into your application, which redirects the user to Twilio to sign in and approve access.
3. Twilio redirects the user back

title: Secure authentication
snippet:
When you create a Twilio account, Twilio generates an [Account SID](/docs/glossary/what-is-a-sid) and an Auth Token. The Auth Token provides broad account access and should be protected like a high-privilege password.
---
## Supported authentication methods
Twilio supports three authentication methods. Choose based on your security requirements and integration needs:
1. **[OAuth 2.0](/docs/iam/oauth-apps/account-oauth-apps) — Recommended for new integrations**
- Short-lived access tokens, as brief as one minute
- Scoped to specific permissions
- Best for third-party apps and delegated access
- Requires token refresh mechanism
2. **[API Keys](/docs/iam/api-keys) — Recommended for server-side apps**
- Main API Key: Provides broad account access (avoid for new integrations)
- Standard API Key: Full account access with SID isolation
- Restricted API Key: Scoped to specific capabilities (recommended for new integrations)
3. **[Auth Token authentication](/docs/iam/api/authtoken) — Legacy option**
- Provides broad account access
- Should only be used when OAuth 2.0 or API keys are not supported
- Treat as last-resort option
---
## Choosing the right authentication method
Whenever the integration supports OAuth 2.0 or a Restricted API Key, use it. These options allow you to scope access to the capabilities your integration needs. This limits the potential impact of a leaked credential.
Auth Tokens and Main API Keys provide broad account access. Although they remain supported, treat them as legacy or last-resort options rather than the default for new integrations.
The following table compares key attributes of each authentication method:
| Method | Scope control | Token lifetime | Recommended use | Security level |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| OAuth 2.0 | Highly scoped | Short-lived (configurable) | Third-party apps, delegated access | Highest |
| Restricted API Key | Scoped to capabilities | Long-lived (until revoked) | Server-side apps | High |
| Standard API Key | Account-level access | Long-lived (until revoked) | Admin access, account management | Medium |
| Auth Token | Broad account access | Long-lived (until rotated) | Legacy integrations only | Low |
---
## OAuth 2.0 and SDK support
OAuth 2.0 provides the strongest security posture for API authentication. To simplify implementation, Twilio provides [SDK support for OAuth](/docs/iam/oauth-apps/oauth-access-token#server-side-sdk-support). These SDKs refresh tokens and reduce the amount of code that you must impl

title: Organization OAuth apps
snippet:
Twilio's organization-level APIs only support OAuth 2.0. API keys and Auth Tokens are not supported.
Organization-level APIs can be accessed using both the [Client Credentials](https://twilio.com/docs/iam/oauth-apps/overview#client-credentials) and [Authorization Code](https://twilio.com/docs/iam/oauth-apps/overview#authorization-code) grant types of OAuth 2.0. The steps below explain how to manage both types of OAuth apps.
---
## Client Credentials
### Create an OAuth app
Twilio ConsoleLegacy Console
1. Log in to [Twilio Console](https://1console.twilio.com/) and navigate to [**Settings** > **Organization settings** > **Organization API access**](https://1console.twilio.com/organization/settings/oauth/apps).
2. Click **Create OAuth application**.
3. For **Grant type**, select **Client credentials**.
4. Enter the **Application name** and **Application description**.
5. On the **Scopes & permissions** step, select the scopes and permission you want to include in the OAuth application. Get the Permission to API mapping details [here](https://twilio.com/docs/iam/oauth-apps/org-oauth-apps#scopespermissions-available-for-organization-oauth-apps).
6. On the **Copy secret** page, copy the credentials and store them somewhere secure.
7. Select the **Got it!** checkbox and click **Finish**.
To generate the access token, use the [Token API](https://twilio.com/docs/iam/oauth-apps/oauth-access-token).
### View or update an OAuth app
Twilio ConsoleLegacy Console
1. Log in to [Twilio Console](https://1console.twilio.com/) and navigate to [**Settings** > **Organization settings** > **Organization API access**](https://1console.twilio.com/organization/settings/oauth/apps).
2. On the **OAuth applications** page, click on the **App name** of the Client Credentials app you want to view or update.
3. On the **APPLICATION DETAILS** tab, view **Application name, Description of the application, Date created** and **Created by**. To update the application details, click **Edit application details** and update the details, then click **Save**.
4. On the **ACCESS SETTINGS**, view **OAuth Scopes**. You can update the **OAuth scopes**.
5. On the **Credentials** tab, view the Client ID with the ability to rotate Client Secret.

title: REST API: OAuth App resource
snippet:
The OAuth App resource only supports account OAuth apps that use the Client Credentials grant type. To generate an access token with an OAuth app's credentials, use the [OAuth Token API](https://twilio.com/docs/iam/oauth-apps/oauth-access-token).
All requests use the base URL `https://iam.twilio.com/v1/Account/OAuthApps`.
You can authenticate requests using either HTTP Basic authentication or OAuth.
For HTTP Basic authentication, use your Account SID and Auth Token or an [API key](https://twilio.com/docs/iam/api-keys) SID and secret.
For OAuth, send an access token from the [OAuth Token API](https://twilio.com/docs/iam/oauth-apps/oauth-access-token) as a Bearer token in the `Authorization` header.
If your request includes a body, it must be formatted as JSON.
---
## OAuth App properties
| Property | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `sid` | string | The unique identifier of the OAuth app, which is also its client ID. Starts with `OQ`. |
| `type` | string | The OAuth grant type of the OAuth app, which is always `Client Credential`. |
| `friendly_name` | string | The name of the OAuth app. |
| `description` | string | A description of the OAuth app. |
| `status` | string | The status of the OAuth app, for example `ACTIVE`. |
| `policy` | object | The permissions granted to the OAuth app. See [Policy object](https://twilio.com/docs/iam/oauth-apps/account-oauth-apps-resource#policy-object). |
| `access_token_ttl` | integer | The length of time in minutes that access tokens issued for the OAuth app remain valid. |
| `date_created` | string | The date and time the OAuth app was created, in ISO 8601 format. |
| `created_by` | string | The email address of the user who created the OAuth app. |
| `creator_sid` | string | The SID of the user who created the OAuth app. Starts with `US`. |
| `secret` | string | The client secret of the OAuth app. Returned when you create, update, or rotate the secret of an OAuth app. Not returned when you fetch or list OAuth apps. |

Must be `Client Credential`. |
| `owner_sid` | string | yes | The SID of the account that owns the OAuth app. Must match the account you authenticate with. |
| `friendly_name` | string | yes | The name of the OAuth app. Maximum 64 characters. |
| `description` | string | no | A description of the OAuth app. Maximum 140 characters. |
| `policy` | object | yes | The permissions to grant the OAuth app. `policy.allow` must contain at least one permission. See [Policy object](https://twilio.com/docs/iam/oau

title: OAuth Token API
snippet:
Access Tokens can be generated by calling the Token API endpoint with the right set of parameters and values. The request differs between Client Credentials and Authorization Code OAuth apps.
---
## Client Credentials Access Token request
`POST https://oauth.twilio.com/v2/token`
**Encoding type**:`application/x-www-form-urlencoded`
#### Request body parameters
| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `client_id` | string | yes | The unique identifier of an OAuth app |
| `client_secret` | string | yes | The confidential secret associated with the client ID |
| `grant_type` | string | yes | Specify the OAuth grant type as `client_credentials` |
#### cURL Request
```
1curl --location 'https://oauth.twilio.com/v2/token' \
2--header 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
3--data-urlencode 'client_id={CLIENT_ID}' \
4--data-urlencode 'client_secret={CLIENT_SECRET}' \
5--data-urlencode 'grant_type=client_credentials'
```
#### Success response
**Status**: `200 OK`
**Body (JSON)**:
```
1{
2    "access_token": "{ACCESS_TOKEN}",
3    "id_token": null,
4    "token_type": "Bearer",
5    "expires_in": 3600,
6    "refresh_token": null
7}
```
**Response Fields**
| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `access_token` | string | The Access Token issued by the authorization server |
| `token_type` | string | The type of token (typically `Bearer`) |
| `expires_in` | integer | The token lifetime in seconds |
---
#### Request body parameters
| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `client_id` | string | yes | The unique identifier of an OAuth app |
| `client_secret` | string | yes | The confidential secret associated with the client ID |
| `grant_type` | string | yes | Specify the OAuth grant type as `authorization_code` |
| `code` | string | yes | Authorization code generated after consent |
| `redirect_uri` | string | yes | The redirect URL of the OAuth app |
#### cURL Request
```
1curl --location 'https://oauth.twilio.com/v2/token' \
2--header 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
3--data-urlencode 'client_id={CLIENT_ID}' \
4--data-urlencode 'client_secret={CLIENT_SECRET}' \
5--data-urlencode 'grant_type=authorization_code' \
6--data-urlencode 'code=AUTHORIZATION_CODE' \
7--data-urlencode 'redirect_uri={REDIRECT_URL}'
```

**Status**: `200 OK`

```
2    "access_token": "{ACCESS_TOKEN}",

title: Authenticate webhooks with OAuth 2.0, Basic, or Digest
snippet:
Your webhook endpoint can require Twilio to authenticate itself as any other API client would. Twilio supports OAuth 2.0 client credentials, HTTP Basic, and HTTP Digest.

Twilio stores credentials in a required [Webhook Setting](/docs/usage/webhooks/webhook-settings) `auth` object in one of two forms.
| Form | When to use it |
|---|---|
| **Inline** (`source: INLINE`) | Each Setting has its own credentials. Recommended for most accounts. |
| **AuthProfile** (`source: REFERENCE`) | Several Settings share one set of credentials, so you rotate them in one place. |
The standalone resource `AuthProfile` stores *one* set of credentials. To access these settings, get the `authProfileId`.
---
## OAuth 2.0
To fetch an access token from your authorization server, Twilio uses the [client credentials flow](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6749#section-4.4). Twilio then sends the token as a [`Bearer` token](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6750#section-2.1) in the `Authorization` header of each webhook. When a token nears expiry, Twilio requests a replacement.
### Prerequisites
An OAuth 2.0 authorization server with client credentials support, and from it:
- The token endpoint URL
- A client ID
- A client secret
- Optionally, a scope
- Optionally, an audience
### Request body parameters
| Field | Necessity | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `scheme` or `type` | required | `OAUTH2`. Use `scheme` for inline credentials, `type` for an AuthProfile. |
| `tokenUrl` | required | Your authorization server's token endpoint. |
| `clientId` | required | The OAuth 2.0 client identifier. |
| `clientSecret` | required | The OAuth 2.0 client secret. Write-only, and never returned in a response. |
| `scope` | optional | The scope Twilio requests. |
| `audience` | optional | The audience Twilio requests. |
| `clientCredentialsAuthMethod` | optional | `CLIENT_SECRET_POST` (default) or `CLIENT_SECRET_BASIC`. |
### Create an OAuth 2.0 AuthProfile
Make a `POST` request to the `AuthProfiles` resource.
```
1curl -X POST https://webhooks.twilio.com/v1/Webhooks/AuthProfiles \
2     -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
3     -u {API_KEY_SID}:{API_KEY_SECRET} \
4     -d '{
5           "type": "OAUTH2",
6           "friendlyName": "Example authorization server",
7           "tokenUrl": "https://auth.example.com/oauth2/token",
8           "clientId": "{CLIENT_ID}",
9           "clientSecret": "{CLIENT_SECRET}",
10           "scope": "webhooks:write",
